stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Radiosondes, small instrument packages carried aloft by weather balloons, report temperature and humidity every few seconds as they rise. On one spring afternoon, forecasters in western Kansas sent up two of them to judge whether storms could still form before dark. Launched just three hours apart from the same field, ______
choices: forecasters recorded a warm layer aloft that had nearly vanished by the second ascent.
the two balloons recorded a warm layer aloft that had nearly vanished by the second ascent.
a warm layer recorded by the first balloon had nearly vanished by the second ascent.
the data from the two balloons showed a warm layer that had nearly vanished by the second ascent.
explanation: Ask what was launched three hours apart. The balloons were. The noun right after the comma has to be the balloons, and only this choice starts with them. The phrase and its subject match.

A.why: You picked the people who launched the balloons. This sentence says the forecasters themselves were launched three hours apart.

C.why: You let the balloon inside the phrase 'recorded by the first balloon' stand in for the subject. The first noun is 'a warm layer', and a layer of air was not launched from a field.

D.why: The word 'balloons' sounded right, so you went with it, but it sits inside 'of/from' phrasing. The real subject is 'the data', and data are not launched.

subtype_name: Dangling modifier: who does the opening phrase describe?

rated_why: Dangling modifier rule, balloons clearly match what was launched

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Hydrologists have read stream gauges in western Wyoming since the 1970s, and their records point to a steady shift in the seasonal rhythm of the region's rivers. Fed almost entirely by snowmelt from the Wind River Range, ______ a change that reflects warmer springs thinning the snowpack earlier each year.
choices: the upper tributaries of the Green River now reaches its peak flow nearly two weeks earlier,
the timing of peak flow in the Green River's upper tributaries has moved nearly two weeks earlier,
the upper tributaries of the Green River now reach their peak flow nearly two weeks earlier,
hydrologists find that the Green River's upper tributaries peak nearly two weeks earlier,
explanation: The streams are fed by snowmelt, so the subject has to be 'the upper tributaries.' That noun is plural, so it needs the plural verb 'reach' and the plural pronoun 'their.' This choice has the right subject and agrees with it.

A.why: The subject is right, but 'River' comes just before the verb and made 'reaches its' sound right. The subject is 'tributaries,' which is plural, so it needs 'reach their.'

B.why: You chose a property of the streams instead of the streams. 'The timing' is the subject here, and timing is not fed by snowmelt.

D.why: You chose the people studying the rivers. This sentence says the hydrologists are fed by snowmelt.

subtype_name: Dangling modifier: who does the opening phrase describe?
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Must verify modifier reference, check plural-verb agreement, and evaluate idiom 'reach/move peak flow'

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: About 33 million years ago, an eruption in what is now central Oregon buried a lakeside forest under drifting volcanic ash. Pressed flat between the fine layers that settled, ______ allowing researchers to estimate the region's ancient rainfall from their size and the shape of their edges.
choices: the ash preserved thousands of the forest's leaves in fine detail,
the eruption left thousands of leaves intact and in fine detail,
paleobotanists have recovered thousands of leaves in fine detail,
thousands of leaves from the forest survived in fine detail,
explanation: The leaves were pressed flat between layers of ash. This choice starts with 'thousands of leaves,' so the phrase describes the right thing. The later 'their size' also refers back to the leaves without any confusion.

A.why: You chose the ash that did the pressing. The ash cannot be pressed between its own layers.

B.why: You chose the event that buried the forest. An eruption is not pressed flat between layers of ash.

C.why: You chose the people who study the fossils. This sentence says the paleobotanists were pressed flat in the ash.

subtype_name: Dangling modifier: who does the opening phrase describe?
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Clear dangling modifier signal: leaves are what was pressed flat

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Before government surveys reached the region, most maps of the Ohio Valley were patchworks of guesswork and hearsay. One of the most influential was engraved by Anselm Vreeland in 1794. Drawn when much of the interior remained unsurveyed, ______ placing several river forks miles from their true positions.
choices: Vreeland's map relied on fur traders' accounts of the region's rivers,
Anselm Vreeland relied on fur traders' accounts of the region's rivers,
fur traders' accounts supplied most of what Vreeland knew of the rivers,
the accuracy of Vreeland's map depended on traders' accounts of the rivers,
explanation: The map is what was drawn. In 'Vreeland's map,' the word 'Vreeland's' only says whose map it is. The subject is 'map,' so the phrase attaches correctly.

B.why: You chose the maker instead of the thing he made. Vreeland drew the map, but he was not drawn himself.

C.why: You chose the source material. The traders' accounts were spoken or written, not drawn while the interior was unsurveyed.

D.why: 'Map' appears, but only inside 'the accuracy of...' The subject is 'accuracy,' and accuracy cannot be drawn.

subtype_name: Dangling modifier: who does the opening phrase describe?
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Must identify what was drawn and trace how it explains the consequent error in placement

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In a feeding study at a university clinic, forty adults were split into two groups and served identical lunches. One group was told to finish within ten minutes, and the other was asked to take at least thirty. Everyone rated their fullness at regular intervals. Compared with participants in the fast group, ______
choices: the lunches eaten slowly produced fullness after about 15 percent fewer calories.
the calorie intake of the slow group was about 15 percent lower when fullness set in.
those in the slow group reported fullness after eating about 15 percent fewer calories.
researchers found the slow group reported fullness after about 15 percent fewer calories.
explanation: A comparison has to put like with like. Participants in the fast group can only be compared with other participants, and this choice starts with 'those in the slow group.'

A.why: You compared people with food. This sentence sets participants against lunches.

B.why: You chose a measurement of the group instead of the group. The subject is 'calorie intake,' and intake is not comparable to participants.

D.why: You chose the people running the study instead of the people in it. This sentence compares the fast-group participants with the researchers.

subtype_name: Dangling modifier: who does the opening phrase describe?
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Comparison structure straightforward once recognizing what is compared to the fast group

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In the early 1900s, the Polish composer Tomasz Wierzbicki spent eighteen months at a sanatorium in the Tatra Mountains, recovering from tuberculosis and forbidden to perform. Composed during that confinement, ______
choices: Wierzbicki wrote three string quartets whose hushed slow movements carry an unusual intimacy.
the unusual intimacy of Wierzbicki's three string quartets is often traced to his long illness.
listeners hear an unusual intimacy in the hushed slow movements of Wierzbicki's quartets.
Wierzbicki's three string quartets contain hushed slow movements that carry an unusual intimacy.
explanation: The quartets are what was composed. In 'Wierzbicki's three string quartets,' the subject is 'quartets,' and 'Wierzbicki's' only says whose they are. So the opening phrase attaches correctly.

A.why: You chose the composer instead of the music. This sentence says Wierzbicki himself was composed.

B.why: 'Quartets' appears, but only inside 'the intimacy of...' The subject is 'intimacy,' which is a quality of the music and was not itself composed.

C.why: You chose the audience instead of the work. This sentence says the listeners were composed in the sanatorium.

subtype_name: Dangling modifier: who does the opening phrase describe?

rated_why: Clear what was composed; dangling modifier rule eliminates distractors quickly

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In 1968, the Japanese American artist Hanae Oda carved a set of cherry-wood blocks depicting the rocky shoreline near her studio in Monterey, California. Printed in an edition of only forty impressions, ______
choices: the woodcut series Tide Tables now rarely appears at auction or in museum shows.
Oda made the woodcut series Tide Tables, which now rarely appears at auction.
collectors rarely find the woodcut series Tide Tables at auction or in museum shows.
the blocks Oda carved for Tide Tables now rarely appear at auction or in museum shows.
explanation: The series of prints is what was printed in an edition of forty. This choice starts with 'the woodcut series Tide Tables,' so the phrase describes the right thing.

B.why: You chose the artist instead of the artwork. This sentence says Oda herself was printed in forty impressions.

C.why: You chose the people who buy the prints. This sentence says the collectors were printed.

D.why: You chose the tool instead of what it made. The blocks were used to print the edition, but the blocks themselves were not printed.

subtype_name: Dangling modifier: who does the opening phrase describe?
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content

adjudication.why: "Printed in an edition of only forty impressions" describes the prints (the woodcut series Tide Tables), not the wooden blocks they were printed from, so D gives the modifier the wrong subject.

rated_why: Multiple grammatically viable answers; must choose most natural parallelism for printed work

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In the summer of 2023, dozens of guests at a lakeside resort came down with stomach illness within days of one another, and the county health department opened an investigation. After tracing the outbreak to a single contaminated ice machine, ______
choices: the source of the outbreak was dismantled and the resort's water lines were flushed.
county health officials had the machine dismantled and the resort's water lines flushed.
the sickened guests learned the machine would be dismantled and the water lines flushed.
the ice machine was dismantled on county orders and the resort's water lines flushed.
explanation: Ask who traced the outbreak. The health officials did, and they are the first noun in this choice. The phrase attaches to the people who did the tracing.

A.why: This choice buries the real idea inside 'the source of...' The subject is 'the source,' and a source cannot trace an outbreak.

C.why: You chose the people who got sick instead of the people who investigated. The guests did not trace the outbreak.

D.why: You chose the thing that was found. This sentence says the ice machine traced the outbreak back to itself.

subtype_name: Dangling modifier: who does the opening phrase describe?
license: CC BY 4.0 - original item, not College Board content
rated_why: Requires reasoning about agency: who logically takes action after health officials trace the source
